description: Two banks of sixteen faders putting out steady voltages on a polyphonic cable, each bank with its own modulation input and a way of sampling values from a cable

params.text: Sets the voltage on this channel of its bank, 0-10V, or -5V to 5V where the bank is switched to bipolar
Switches this bank between putting out 0-10V and putting out -5V to 5V
Scales this bank's modulation input, -1 to 1, so that a negative setting inverts it; with nothing patched to IN, it sets how far a sample randomises the faders
Copies the IN voltages into this bank's faders; with nothing patched to IN it randomises them instead
Sets how many channels this bank puts out, 1 to 16; the faders past that count are left out

inputs.text: The voltage added to this bank's faders, one channel per fader; a cable with fewer channels than the bank is wrapped round from the first channel again
A further modulation for this bank, multiplied into the IN voltage channel by channel before the mod-scaling knob is applied
A rising edge copies the IN voltages into this bank's faders; with a polyphonic cable here, each channel triggers its own fader

outputs.text: This bank's faders as a polyphonic cable, one channel per fader in use

notes: hold Alt while dragging across the faders to set several of them in one movement.
the menu carries a separate SAMPLE mode, POLY channel and view setting for each of the two banks, under the headings A and B.
menu: update cycle — sets how many samples pass between one recalculation and the next, 1 to 1024
SAMPLE mode: IN absolute (default), IN relative (with MODS) — chooses whether a sample copies the IN voltages as they arrive or copies the faders as they stand after modulation
set POLY channels by: POLY button (default), IN port (auto), IN port (on SAMPLE trigger) — chooses whether the channel count follows the POLY button or the channels arriving at IN
view mode: faders (default), staves in C, Psilocybe Omrinsis, windows — chooses how the bank is drawn

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
